text_decisions: The Paippalāda field is the modern TEI text. Both lines transmit vāhāñ in connected speech before chunaṃ, read here as underlying plural vāhān. Only the second TEI line marks it sic. Whitney reports the distinct Paippalāda reading vāhaṁ (accusative singular) and kenāśo. Keep that report in its own witness field.
The selected Devanāgarī Maitrāyaṇī text writes long ī, where Whitney’s comparison prints short i. Agreement of singular etu with one ploughman survives this difference.
In the Ṛgveda fourth pāda, dhattam addresses two. Sāyaṇa supplies a verb of watering for the separate Parjanya clause. In the Ṛgveda text only the words originally present count as tokens.

At Vājasaneyi 12.69 the unaccented transcription ends in kartanāsme; the accented presentation on the same page prints kartanāsmai. Mahīdhara discusses the plural-looking verb with the two addressees. The alignment of the earlier animal clause uses neither final reading as a deciding condition.
Both Paippalāda locations agree in the first two lines and diverge in the latter two. At 2.22.3d the plants are the subject of plural santu. The farmer’s clause has moved to pāda a at both locations.
bound: The sources license whole constructions. Interchanging a preverb, case ending, word order or number across rows would create additional requests without a witness. Inflectional and clause projection are written comparisons. They add no finite-grid credit.
